pending_commit.commit_message: cros_ec: Add I2C and LPC probe methods for CrOS EC This patch adds the I2C and LPC methods as fallbacks in cros_ec_setup() and updates platforms to use it. Since Daisy, Spring and Skate fallback to raw I2C they still need a custom setup function to hook up I2C address structs in the private data. Link, Slippy, and Rambi fallback to raw IO, but since the IO addresses for that are standard in generic CrOS EC LPC code we don't need to do anything special and can remove ec.c for those boards. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=tested "mosys ec info" on veyron_mighty, paine (would be nice to test on daisy, spring, or snow as well...) Signed-off-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Change-Id: I2ea1171a93b5fcf761f742be2e95047b2bd12b2b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431520 Commit-Ready: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org>

cros_ec: Clean-up internal and public interfaces When CrOS EC was first added the board code did a lot of the work and a lot of functionality had to be exposed. Now that we've standardized and consolidated things we can clean-up the "public" API used by board-level code and limit scope of most lowlevel functions. A new header, cros_ec_internal.h, is created to contain the "private" API for functions which are called among the drivers. And while we're at it, move cros_ec_lock.h since it should not be needed outside the CrOS EC drivers. This patch opportunistically removes cros_ec_hello() which isn't used. Also, since the probe functions set up the EC/PD interfaces we can rename them to imply setup (cros_ec_probe_* -> cros_ec_setup_*). BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=compiled for amd64 and arm-generic Change-Id: I6ba94f9cd1cecd2fd0403717afab804a8db56c7c Signed-off-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/434317 Commit-Ready: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org>

drm-tests: linear_bo_test: stop using alpha format for framebuffers This test more closely matches the behavior of Chrome in that it will allocate a BGRA format buffer object but make a framebuffer from that BO as BGRX. This fixes the issue where newer (4.4) i915 drivers will reject BGRA framebuffers on baytrail devices, causing linear_bo_test to indicate failure. This test also adds the bs_drm_fb_builder class for building drm framebuffers from gbm buffer objects with tweaks like format. BUG=chromium:644338 TEST=On kevin: kill permission_broker, set up device_jail_utility server. Use lsusb -t to find a device with an attached kernel driver, i.e. btusb, add a jail for it In python: >>> f = open("/dev/jailed-189-XXX", "rb") Choose "detach" in the server. Check syslog, lsusb -t again to make sure the driver was detached. In python: >>> f.close() Ensure the driver is reattached. (If using btusb you can also check visually that the bluetooth menu disables itself when you detach the driver, and re-enables itself when you attach it again.)
